House Bill 571 (COMMITTEE SUBSTITUTE) By: Representatives Hawkins of The Senate Committee on Regulated Industries and Utilities offered the 27th, Jasperse of the 11th, Dempsey of the 13th, Jackson of the 128th, Silcox of the 53rd, and others following substitute to HB 571:
A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT
To amend Chapter 34 of Title 43 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to physicians, assistants, and others, so as to provide for the licensing of radiologist assistants; to … the radiologist and may include injecting diagnostic agents to sites other than intravenous, performing diagnostic aspirations and localizations, and assisting radiologists with other invasive procedures, according to levels of supervision as defined by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services. Such radiologist assistant may with general supervision perform other noninvasive procedures unless said procedures are expressly restricted by the board to not be performed by radiologist assistants under general supervision. Such radiologist assistant may also perform other procedures under general supervision as may be authorized by the board.
43-34-332. A person shall be qualified for licensure as a radiologist assistant and the board may shall issue a license if that person: (1) Has applied in writing in form and substance satisfactory to the board and is at least 21 years of age; (2) Has not engaged in conduct or activities which would constitute grounds for discipline under this article; (3) Is … seeking renewal of licensure under this article to complete board approved continuing education; (2) Establish the number of hours of continuing education to be completed as well as the categories in which the continuing education is to be completed; and (3) Maintain continued certification and registration as a radiologist assistant with the American Registry of Radiologic technologist or radiology practitioner assistant with the Certification Board for Radiology Practitioner Assistants and the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists. (c) A person who has permitted his or her license to expire or who has had his or her license on inactive status may have his or … active duty within the armed forces of the United States or with the state militia and called into service or training; or (2) In training or education under the supervision of the United States preliminary to induction into military service may have his or her license renewed or restored without paying a lapsed renewal fee if, within two years after termination from the service, training, or education except under conditions other than honorable, he or she furnishes the board with satisfactory evidence that he or she has been so engaged and that his or her service, training, or education has been terminated.
43-34-334. (a) On and after July 1, 2025, 2026, a person shall not engage in the scope of practice for radiologist assistants in this state without a valid license issued by the board pursuant to this article. (b) A person shall not hold himself or herself out as a … license as a radiologist assistant. (c) A person who verifies to the board that he or she is employed in this state as a radiologist assistant as of the effective date of this article shall by operation of law be licensed authorized to practice as a radiologist assistant in this state on or after July 1, 2025. 2026, contingent upon such individual having applied with the board for appropriate licensure.
43-34-335. (a) A radiologist may use the services of a radiologist assistant under the on site direct supervision of such radiologist, provided that such radiologist assistant is duly qualified and licensed pursuant to this article. (b) Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this Code section, a radiologist assistant may with general supervision perform other noninvasive procedures unless said procedures are expressly restricted by the board to not be performed by radiologist assistants under general supervision. Such radiologist assistant may also perform other procedures under general supervision as may be authorized by the board. (c) A radiologist assistant shall not interpret images, make diagnoses, or prescribe medications or therapies. (c) (d) Any rules and regulations adopted by the board pertaining to the scope of practice as a radiologist assistant in this state shall be consistent with guidelines adopted by the American College of Radiology, the American Society of Radiologic Technologists, the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists, or any other entity deemed appropriate by the board.
43-34-336. The board shall have the power and responsibility to: (1) Determine the qualifications and fitness of applicants for licensure and renewal of licensure; (2) … Members shall receive no compensation for service on the committee. The committee shall have such advisory duties and responsibilities as the board may determine, including, but not limited to, consulting with the board on the issuance, denial, suspension, and revocation of licenses and the promulgation of rules and regulations under this article. The initial members of the advisory committee may include persons eligible for licensing under this article. Subsequent advisory committee members must be licensed pursuant to this article.

SECTION 5. All laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act are repealed.
